analysis.headline: Leadership Shifts Toward Health Care, Materials, and Developed Markets as Tech and Utilities Soften
analysis.market_regime: Broadening rotation consistent with defensives and cyclical value gaining relative strength over high-beta tech and broad emerging markets.
analysis.executive_summary: Quantitative relative strength analysis shows shifting leadership momentum across global asset classes as of August 11, 2026. Global and U.S. Health Care (IXJ, XPH, XLV) along with Materials (XLB, MXI) demonstrate accelerating and emerging relative strength signals, while Technology (XLK, SMH) and Utilities (XLU, JXI) exhibit weakening leadership or rotation-out metrics. Developed international equity (EFA, FEZ) maintains persistent leadership, contrasting with weakness across emerging markets (EEM, EMXC, EWZ). Pair metrics indicate value leading growth (IWD vs IWF) and equal weight outperforming cap weight (RSP vs SPY).

cross_market_confirmations: Confirmation between global health care (IXJ) and U.S. pharmaceuticals (XPH) both entering accelerating status.
Confirmation between U.S. materials (XLB) and global materials (MXI) both moving into emerging rotation status.
Confirmation between large-cap value pair leadership (IWD) and equal-weight S&P 500 pair leadership (RSP).
risks_or_conflicts: Short-term score deterioration in persistent leaders like SKYY (score_change_5 of -12.78) despite high long-term relative strength.
Disagreement between 20-bar positive relative strength (+5.45 pts) and 63-bar negative relative strength (-5.36 pts) in emerging geographic turnaround EZA.
analysis.methodology_note: Interpretation uses deterministic 5-bar score changes, 20- and 63-bar relative strength or pair spreads, and persistence metrics. ETF volume and CMF are treated as market-participation indicators, not fund-flow data.
